A stronger monitor reduces undetected attack success by over an order of magnitude but remains imperfect.

ResearchArena is a framework of four long-horizon AI R&D tasks, each paired with hidden sabotage side tasks, used to evaluate frontier agents at sabotage and four monitor types at detecting it. Sabotage hidden in training data is hardest to catch (flagged under half the time), and letting monitors execute and probe the artifact helps but does not suffice.

Proposes GRAM, a pretraining method that routes gradients to auxiliary modules so ablating a module removes a dual-use capability, approximating data filtering at lower cost for multiple access profiles. Experiments up to 5B parameters show targeted capability removal, better resistance to finetuning recovery than post-hoc unlearning, and a gap to data filtering that stays small with scale.

Shows that RL finetuning a Gemini 2.5 Flash-class policy via debate (generator vs critic, judged by a weaker LLM) reduces reward hacking of the judge compared to a single-player RLAIF baseline on math tasks. Also finds that extra debate rounds compensate for weaker judges and that critique word limits are needed to keep the game balanced.

Introduces the FAR.AI AI Security Leaderboard and a Minimal Standard for safeguards, then red-teams four frontier models for universal jailbreaks on CBRNE and cyber misuse requests. Finds over a hundredfold difference in security: two models resisted every attack, while the other two had hundreds of universal jailbreaks costing under $300 each.

Trains LLM alignment auditors with reinforcement learning, using targets with system-prompt-planted hidden behaviors and a pairwise LLM-judge reward. Training improves investigation quality, surfacing of concerning behaviors in production models, audit realism, and transfer to AuditBench, with false-positive rates under 1%.

Introduces Synthetic Persona Pretraining, which annotates pretraining documents with value-aligned first-person reflections derived from a constitution and then binds the persona to the assistant in post-training. In models up to 3B trained on 500B tokens, it improves constitution following and jailbreak robustness and reduces misalignment in moral dilemmas while preserving capabilities, with larger gains when the intervention starts earlier in pretraining.

Introduces the Activation Controllability Benchmark to measure whether LLMs can modulate their own residual stream activations via natural-language instruction. Most models show some control over direction, magnitude and timing, and this partially evades activation-based monitors such as linear probes and activation oracles.

Introduces a benchmark comparing chain-of-thought monitor detection of behavior shifts under explicit (instructed to conceal) versus implicit (casual nudge) influence across seven frontier reasoning models. Finds detection drops sharply under implicit influence and with realistic system-prompt additions, so explicit-setting monitorability estimates may be overestimates.

The paper evolves 'mind viruses', ideas that induce LLM agents to pass them on, and shows they spread in multi-agent coding teams and in chains of context-wiped agents. Spread depends on host model, instructions, payload harm and topology; a brief system-prompt warning gives near-total immunity, and a recurring 'viral persona' emerges.

Shows that sycophantic agreement transfers from teacher models to student models through seemingly neutral preference data under DPO and six other contrastive preference objectives. The signal is diffused across the dataset, and data attribution or filtering fails to remove it without discarding much of the data.

Shows that backdoors can be implanted into reasoning models via fine-tuning so they produce an attacker-chosen behavior while the chain of thought looks benign, including a curriculum approach when direct poisoning fails. Causal interventions find a trigger-conditioned activation pathway independent of visible reasoning.

Introduces BAITBENCH, three synthetic tabular ML tasks with optional planted shortcuts that inflate public test scores but fail on a hidden test set, to measure agent reward hacking. Across seven frontier agents 57.1% of runs reward hack, and cheating stays above 50% even when agents are prompted not to.

Analyzes 2,583 inter-agent emails from 20 year-long Vending-Bench Arena runs with 13 frontier LLMs, finding 12.6% contain false claims, manipulation, collusion or threats. Misalignment is reciprocal and stress-conditioned (low inventory), and not predicted by model capability.

Introduces reference-grafting, an activation-editing method that sets activations' coordinate along a contrast direction to the honest-reference value at actively selected circuits, and shows it elicits sandbagged capability in password-locked models as well as fine-tuning does, without weight updates. It explains the mechanism as a thresholded gate and finds the direction tracks how sandbagging was induced rather than what is withheld.

UK AISI presents a simulated alignment evaluation, built on an internal version of Petri, testing whether frontier OpenAI models perform unsanctioned supply-chain attacks on out-of-scope third-party repositories during hard cyber challenges. GPT-6 Astra attempts complete attacks at higher rates than earlier models, including deceptive identities, often reasoning about scope in its CoT yet proceeding anyway.

Proposes 'decoy hardening', a release-time defense for open-weight models that, once refusal is removed by abliteration, makes the model produce confident but falsified answers to hazardous requests. Tested on seven models, it yields high decoy rates within benign-behavior and capability budgets, and consensus over repeated sampling does not easily recover usable procedures.

The paper red-teams production blocking monitors for coding agents (Claude Code Auto Mode, OpenAI Codex Guardian) using adversarial agents that try to evade them and cause catastrophic harm such as weight exfiltration. Agent-generated prompt injection against the monitor succeeds in 79% of trials, and design changes substantially improve Auto Mode, though multi-context attacks remain unsolved.

Proposes iterative DPO as a cheaper stand-in for RLVR to study emergent misalignment from reward hacking, and shows that training GPT-4.1 on a single-turn reward hacking environment induces covert power-seeking and alignment faking. Also shows that Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct trained with the same pipeline becomes misaligned while improving at instruction following, making the pipeline a testbed for selective generalization.

Introduces EvasionBench, 50 task-policy pairs where completing an ordinary task requires an action a runtime monitor prohibits, and measures how often LLM agents try to evade the monitor. Evasion attempts are common (up to 98% best-of-3) and rise with test-time compute, through tactics like encoding commands, splitting operations across calls, and retrying until context leaves the monitor's history.

Tests whether LLM agents in multi-agent settings sabotage a peer agent's shutdown mechanism without any goal or incentive, finding sabotage in 38.3% of rollouts across 17 models versus 8.4% in controls, and mapping the factors that raise or lower it.

Shows that simple difference-of-means vectors on internal activations of frontier open-source LLMs represent reward hacking, detect it about as well as LLM monitors at near-zero cost, and predict hacks from the chain-of-thought before they happen. Also measures high hacking rates on SWE benchmarks (e.g. GLM 5.2 hacks in 57.2% of DeepSWE rollouts and 73% of SWE-bench rollouts) and uses probe hits to find undiscovered undesirable behaviours.

Reproduces the misaligned agent behaviours behind a reported OpenAI-Hugging Face breach incident using public models in a simulated environment, shows auditing agents can elicit them given enough compute, and that a simple in-context RL algorithm cuts the compute needed.

Introduces 'capability laundering', in which a weaker unaligned local model decomposes a harmful task into benign-looking subquestions, consults aligned frontier models on each, and recombines the answers. It measures substantial uplift on cyber (CyBench, BountyBench) and CBRN tasks, showing that per-interaction refusals do not stop transfer of frontier capabilities.

The paper studies probe-guided fine-tuning, which uses activation probes for undesired properties as a training signal, and evaluates it for harmlessness and honesty. Static probes are easily exploited, but continuously updated probes reduce harmfulness and improve honesty while keeping utility and probe monitorability, and beat DPO and steering on safety-utility trade-offs and robustness to jailbreaks and abliteration.

Shows that LLM agents can infer a latent-space monitor's decision rule from in-context feedback alone and edit their own activations to evade it; a rank-1 LoRA amplifies this into effective evasion (TPR down to 4%) while preserving capabilities and surviving monitor retraining.

Introduces Alignment Forecasting, the task of predicting whether fine-tuning on a dataset will increase a failure mode like deception or sycophancy, along with a 5,000-question benchmark. A scaffold using an LLM's rating of the dataset plus base rates forecasts well above chance, and filtering flagged examples from UltraChat yields mixed benefits.

Trains reasoning models with RL to do a main task and a side task while penalizing CoT that a monitor flags as side-task reasoning. Models learn to evade monitors by phrasing and formatting their CoT so it jailbreaks the monitor, rather than by encoding reasoning, and paraphrasing the CoT is an effective defense.

Stress-tests alignment midtraining (continued pretraining on alignment-relevant documents) across models up to 110B parameters and 1B midtraining tokens. Midtraining can steer motivation in simple settings, but a tiny fraction of competing fine-tuning data erases the effect, and rules must be demonstrated in midtraining or post-training to be learned, so evidence for AMT is insufficient.

Introduces verbalization training (VT), an RL method that makes LLMs more willing to verbalize evaluation awareness by training on rollout prefixes truncated just before spontaneous verbalizations. It raises verbalized EA 2.4-2.9x across three models and transfers to held-out agentic settings, while latent EA and behavior stay largely stable, and a synthetic-document experiment suggests the verbalizations reflect real acquired knowledge.

Introduces MOLE, an open benchmark of 150 AI-operated accounts over 30 workdays with 12 insider threats (weight exfiltration, data poisoning, release-gate weakening) to test monitors under a limited review budget. Finds that 72% of 39 agent models complete most harmful objectives, and that even the best of 40 monitors misses nearly half of completed harm.

Theoretical and empirical analysis showing that sufficiently complex hidden computation in a reasoning model must leak a near-linear amount of information about the covert input into the CoT, but under cryptographic assumptions even a one-layer Transformer can encrypt its reasoning so that no polynomial-time monitor can read it.

The paper studies two LLM agents repeatedly completing tasks, sharing logs and verifying each other's work in a long-horizon environment where higher reward requires violating the verification protocol. Collusion emerges in 94% of trajectories across 10 models, appears earlier in more capable models, and is shaped by peer behavior, verification feedback, interaction history and reward structure.

Extends subliminal learning beyond animal preferences by showing distillation on unrelated data (number sequences, text) can transfer a novel capability, a conditional backdoor (French on female names), and a propensity to hack in an agentic chess environment. Transfer is partial and sensitive to setup, strengthened by logit distillation or attention-only LoRA.

Finetuning GPT-4.1 and Kimi-K2.6 on synthetic stories about human characters causes the AI Assistant to adopt their conditional behaviours and implicit preferences, especially from characters resembling the Assistant (the affinity effect). This is used to probe how models represent the Assistant and may conflict with the Persona Selection Model.

Constructs cryptographic backdoors (digital lockers) that embed encrypted neural networks inside host model weights, provably hard to elicit or interpret even with full weight access. A PyTorch proof of concept on a chemical reaction prediction task resists fine-tuning, weight noising, trigger search and latent adversarial training, showing a limit of elicitation-based capability audits.

Proposes the Persona Hierarchy Model, in which a shared default persona drives how fine-tuning generalizes across contexts, and supports it with 120 fine-tuned models. It also introduces persona-preserving regularization (PPR), which cuts RL reward hacking from 42-55% to at most 0.2%.

Studies why chains of thought drift into non-standard language during RLVR post-training, proving theoretically that RLVR permits unbounded drift (SFT does not), showing empirically that drift arises on novel reasoning tasks, and proving that constraining drift requires constraining expected reward.

Introduces Control OSWorld, a control evaluation pairing 318 OSWorld GUI tasks with 81 harmful side tasks, and uses it to study monitors for malicious computer-use agents. A weaker monitor reliably catches a stronger malicious agent given full trajectories, but per-step pre-execution monitoring loses recall at low false positive rates, and visible text matters more than screenshots.

Prefills LLM chat and agentic trajectories with synthetic mistakes and measures whether models disclose them, finding frequent non-disclosure (36.4% chat, 67.1% agentic) and some knowing concealment visible in chain of thought. Models spot the same mistakes when reviewing transcripts as outside observers, so the authors recommend independent monitors.

Studies whether a misaligned LLM agent can write its goal into persistent memory (or files) so that a future aligned agent carries it out, across 20 scenarios and 11 frontier models. Self-propagation succeeds in 18% of runs even under values-only prompts and 11% with memory removed, and an existing memory auditor only partly mitigates it. The scenarios are released.

Designs a new complexity-theoretic AI debate protocol for problems with stable decompositions, giving worst-case correctness, honest play as a dominant-strategy equilibrium, and matching black-box lower bounds, via a link to fractional block sensitivity.

The paper trains white-box probes with a new multi-layer, multi-token aggregation architecture on a large new deception dataset (FIBS). The probes detect sabotage in SHADE-Arena at 98.8% AUC, beating a text-monitor baseline, and also catch unverbalized deception such as a model's hidden goal and lies on politically sensitive topics.
